summary: Laab khua is cooked Northern Thai minced meat seasoned with a dark, aromatic toasted-spice blend; it is quite different from the sour, fresh-herb Isan larb many visitors know. Huen Phen’s official menu lists pork laab khua, making it an easy Old City or Nimman example.
whyGo: Taste a defining Lanna meat dish whose flavor comes from local spices such as makhwaen (prickly ash), rather than lime and toasted rice.
Order it with sticky rice and other small northern dishes to compare its savory, warm spice profile with more familiar Thai salads.
bestFor: Curious omnivores who enjoy minced meat and assertive, aromatic seasoning.
A shared Northern Thai meal; laab khua is one dish among a broader spread.
skipIf: Vegetarians, vegans, or anyone avoiding meat: the named Huen Phen version is pork.
Anyone avoiding chili or uncertain meat handling; ask for the cooked version and discuss heat and ingredients before ordering.
duration: Allow about 45–75 minutes for a casual meal; this is a planning estimate, not a venue guarantee.
cost: Budget roughly ฿100–300 per person for laab khua with rice and a drink at a casual local restaurant (estimate; check the current menu). Huen Phen’s online price listings vary by branch and do not confirm a current price for this dish.
hours: Huen Phen Old City: daily 08:30–16:30 and 17:00–22:00. Nimman branch: daily 09:00–22:00. Confirm close to travel as December hours may change.
bestTime: Lunch or early dinner gives the best chance of ordering from a full menu; go outside the busiest meal window if you prefer a quieter table. December is a busy visitor season, so allow extra time.
gettingThere: Huen Phen’s Old City branch is at 112 Phra Sing, near Wat Chedi Luang; walk from nearby Old City sights or take a metered/taxi-app ride. The Nimman branch is at 2 Nimmanhaemin Road, Soi 5. Use the branch name in navigation and confirm the pin before setting out.
booking: A walk-in meal is usually practical, but no booking policy for December 2026 is published. For a group or peak dinner, contact the chosen branch using the phone number on its official branch page.
accessibility: The restaurant pages do not publish step-free access, accessible toilets, or seating details. Contact the branch ahead if mobility access matters; street-level layouts and entrances can vary.
practicalTips: Ask for ‘laab khua moo’ (ลาบคั่วหมู) for pork, and clarify ‘cooked’ if needed; northern laab can also be served raw at specialist laab shops.
The toasted spice blend can be pungent and chili-forward. Ask whether the kitchen can reduce chili, though the underlying spice flavor is part of the dish.
It is a meat dish and may be prepared with animal blood or offal depending on the cook; ask about ingredients for dietary, religious, or allergy needs. Cross-contact details are not published.
Sticky rice and fresh vegetables help round out the dish. Huen Phen’s menu includes other Northern dishes if someone in the group wants a non-meat choice.
decemberNotes: December 2026 branch hours and menus are not yet guaranteed. Chiang Mai is in a busy dry-season visitor period; check same-week opening information, expect possible waits at meal times, and confirm whether laab khua is available that day.
uncertainties: No reliable official December 2026 price or serving size for laab khua was found; the per-person budget is an estimate.
Menu presence is verified at Huen Phen, but stock, spice adjustment, ingredients, booking, and accessibility must be confirmed directly.
